correctness.rationale: The finite core is exhaustive: all 3000 maps of ranks 2, 3, and 4 and all 45 pairs of distinct 2-subsets are checked by exact reverse BFS on the simultaneous subset-pair graph. Every instance reaches a distinguishing state, with exact maximum shortest length 9. An independently organized symmetry-reduced engine checks 120 double-rotation transformation representatives and 9 pair-orbit representatives by explicit monoid generation. The classification step is then deductive: every primitive degree-5 group is transitive, hence has order divisible by 5 and contains a 5-cycle; strong sync-maximality is monotone upward; the published converse strong implies primitive completes the equivalence.

value.rationale: The source explicitly asks for the precise class of strongly sync-maximal groups. Degree 5 is the first prime degree where the smallest transitive group is a nontrivial regular cyclic group. Showing that this minimal group already satisfies the universal strong condition yields a complete degree-5 classification, not an isolated witness, and demonstrates that very high transitivity is unnecessary in the strongest possible degree-5 sense.
